text: Íte, also called Ita, Íta, Mo-Íde, or Míde, was an Irish saint. She was a Christian woman of the sixth century C.E. Legends about her are full of pagan motifs. She founded a convent called Cill Íte, now Killeedy, in Co. Limerick. Like the Kildare nun Brigit, Íte seems almost mythological. Her name may have been that of a goddess with whom she was conflated. Her chamber shone as though on fire. She cured a man by removing his horse's ears. Most important, she owned the mythological Cow of abundance, the Glas Ghaibhleann. Her miracles let her control the weather and the flight of birds. This links her to the earth goddesses of the Munster region where she lived.
objective: Document Íte as a legendary Irish saint.
